correctness.rationale: Enumerate 120 matrices in SL(2,F5) and all 7021 unordered two-element normalized supports {1,x,y}. Simultaneous conjugation and reanchoring partitions them into precisely 62 nonoverlapping orbits, each left-translation invariant in rank. Integer regular-convolution matrices have exactly three unit entries in each row. For each orbit representative the four claimed independently primality-checked primes give coinciding modular ranks; product exceeds 3^60, the universal Hadamard bound on every 120x120 square minor. Hence any larger minor zero modulo all primes must vanish over Z, while a rank-size nonzero modular minor survives in characteristic zero. The 62 orbits yield 35 quotient-order triples and exactly {0:159240,4:38400,5:28800,10:28800,20:14400,22:7200,30:2400,40:1200,80:400} supports, 280840 total and 121600 singular. The 400 supports with 80-dimensional kernel are cosets of the ten order-3 subgroups (40 cosets each). Read complete check.cpp and its exact group, orbit, rank logic. An independently coded numba group algorithm exhaustively reproduced all 62 orbits, 35 signatures and four-prime ranks and histogram, not just an old log. The complete finite domain is proved by exhaustive exact certificate; no infinite-family claim.

value.rationale: The binary icosahedral group is the canonical nontrivial perfect central cover of A5, a natural group for finite noncommutative harmonic analysis. Exhaustively determining all unweighted 3-tap convolution kernels by intrinsic quotient orders, with a distinctive 22-nullity stratum and extremal cosets, supplies a reusable exact invariant in a natural nonabelian example; general group-wide theorem not required.

limitations: Precisely 3 distinct unit-coefficient support elements, complex group algebra of SL(2,F5); weighted taps or other binary polyhedral groups not classified.
No general theorem that order signatures suffice in other groups.
